evidence_text:
asc-i6z closed, commit d5c84f7. Two false-green test gaps closed without changing any behaviour: the tests were wrong, not the code.

Gap 1, the doubled warning prefix. Both tests asserted not.toContain('warning: ') -- the absence of the wrong string -- and never that a Warning: appears. Deleting the prefix, or the whole this.warn loop, left both green. They now assert the rendered line: the prefix at the start, and exactly one warning: in it.

Gap 2, the missing-operand test. It asserted only status === 2, and oclif fills a missing positional argument from stdin, so the defective path -- the piped document read AS A FILENAME -- also exits 2 on the resulting ENOENT. One exit code, two opposite behaviours, and the test named for the distinction could not draw it. It pipes a real document now and asserts the discriminator: the Missing 1 required arg message, no ENOENT, no could not be read, and nothing registered.

The define half of the piped-value block below had become an exact duplicate of that test once it was strengthened, so it was folded into it rather than left asserting the same thing twice. Its ENOENT and nothing-was-registered assertions moved up with it; coverage is unchanged and the two tests are now one.

Measured, not assumed: the doubled import line reads Warning: <path>: warning: ... because import renders the source path between the prefix and the message. The case-sensitive version of the new count assertion survived a faithful reintroduction of the import half of the defect; the case-insensitive version fires. Five mutations total, all five fire, both sources restore byte-identical.

Gates: format, typecheck, lint, 1211 passing with 2 pre-existing skips, align green.

NOT CLAIMED: that the assertion count is stable against arbitrary warning text. It counts the word warning: in the rendered line, so a store warning whose own prose contains that word would fail it. The fixtures here are ours and fixed, and the store's vocabulary-check message does not contain it; a future warning that does would need the assertion narrowed to the prefix position.

packages/cli/skill/commands/ascend-analyze.md, 16 lines, deliberately thin: it takes the type name(s) as $ARGUMENTS and drives the skill's method rather than restating it. Keeping the judgement in one place is the point -- a command that duplicated the method would be a second thing to keep in step with the flags, and the drift guard covers both files precisely because neither is allowed to become the other's copy. Landed in 3b57e8c with the gate green: 81 test files, 1,794 passed, 2 skipped.

The six-step method (profile -> sample -> cluster -> hand-label -> back-test -> commit the pass) ships as packages/cli/skill/ascend-analysis/SKILL.md, installed by the new `asc install-skill`. It lives under the package rather than at the repo root because npm `files` publishes package-internal paths only. Both halves of the bead are met: it teaches the method, and it doubles as a recall surface at both ends -- it opens by telling the reader to run bare `asc` so a type they did not know about cannot become a population they silently excluded, and it closes by routing the finished analysis back into the corpus as an evidence_record or a decision, including a rule that was back-tested and REJECTED. Every flag it cites is checked against the live oclif manifest by skill-drift.test.ts, mutation-tested three ways (bogus flag, bogus command, missing skill directory), so the citations are a red test rather than a promise. Landed in 3b57e8c with the gate green: 81 test files, 1,794 passed, 2 skipped.

properties.stage: E12.4a — the migration, and the archive

evidence_text:
Started, not finished: the operation exists and the whole gate is green, but it has no production caller yet.

Built: packages/store/src/migrate.ts (migrateStoreToTree, 9 tests) turns a SQLite store into a record tree through openRecordWriter, verifies by reading the tree back as a SET of canonical lines before moving anything, and archives the database plus its -wal/-shm as one unit. Every refusal fires before any write, so a failed run strands no half-tree. The report names every table holding rows no corpus line can carry, derived from sqlite_master rather than listed (ingest_cursor and the meta keys, on this repo's shape).

Also: corpusLines moved from packages/cli/src/commands/export.ts into packages/store/src/corpus-lines.ts, so the export and the migration share one spelling of 'a store, as lines'. export.ts lost 130 lines and changed no behaviour; corpus.ts's shim re-exports it.

Gate at the transition: prettier, tsc -b, tsc -p tsconfig.eslint.json, eslint, align check all green; vitest run 117 files, 2742 passed | 2 skipped.

Remaining: no command surface (deferred deliberately -- the plan does not say whether the cutover is a new `asc migrate` or folded into `asc init`), and nothing yet names .ascend-archived/ for the archive, which the function leaves to its caller.

writeLines exists (packages/store/src/jsonl-index.ts) with 8 tests in packages/store/test/index-write.test.ts, and the whole gate is green: prettier, tsc -b, tsc -p tsconfig.eslint.json, eslint, align check (verdict: green, 0 violations, 20 baselined), vitest run 118 files, 2750 passed | 2 skipped (2752).

The ordering claim is VERIFIED BY MUTATION rather than argued. A faithful reversal -- replay in both branches, append afterwards -- failed exactly one test, 'leaves the tree written and the index stale when the replay refuses the line', and passed the other seven: 1 failed | 7 passed. So the refused-replay test is the single place where the order is load-bearing, and the test file says so with that number.

The writable index handle is private to jsonl-index.ts and reachable from one caller, the same construction buildIndex has; openIndex stays read-only, so 'a read never builds' is still structural rather than conventional.

Two behaviours only building it settled: a foreign file at index.db refuses the write BEFORE the append (ForeignStoreError propagates out of the currency check), because a tree written while the index cannot be touched would be records no read of the project can see; and the not-current branch RETURNS stale:true rather than throwing, because the write itself succeeded -- the JSONL is the store.

This stage reverses EV-32's 'no incremental path'. EV-32 concluded wholesale-or-nothing from a cold rebuild of 3.02 s; EV-33 measured 40.27 s at 10x, which kills wholesale-on-write (3.39 s per asc record, EV-34 at 6,404 entries) while leaving the rest of the design standing. The module doc's 'Wholesale-or-nothing, and why there is no incremental path' section was rewritten rather than left contradicting the code.
